PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_INSTR.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.error: Puts the title block at the top.

example.question: Where is the title block of a drawing sheet?
example.correct_answer: At the bottom right

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.cause: Titles in books and essays are at the top, so the learner puts the title block there.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.reveals: Offer "At the top left" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.help: Look at a real drawing sheet: the title block is at the bottom right, where it can be read when sheets are folded or filed.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.feedback: The title block is at the bottom right of the sheet.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.error: Leaves out the border, thinking the edge of the paper is enough.

example.question: Why is a border drawn on a drawing sheet?
example.wrong_answer: It is not needed; the paper edge is enough
example.correct_answer: It frames the drawing and leaves a margin for handling and filing

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.cause: The edge of the paper seems to be a frame already.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.reveals: Offer "It is not needed; the paper edge is enough" beside "It frames the drawing and leaves a margin for handling and filing" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.help: Draw a border 10 mm inside the edges; explain it frames the drawing and leaves a margin for handling and filing.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.feedback: The border is a frame drawn inside the edges of the sheet.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.error: Gives A3's size, 420 by 297 mm, for A4.

example.question: What is the size of A4?
example.correct_answer: 297 by 210 millimetres

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.cause: A3 and A4 are learnt together, and the learner gives the larger size.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.reveals: Offer "420 by 297 millimetres" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.help: Fold an A3 sheet in half: it makes two A4 sheets. Measure: A4 is 297 by 210 mm.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.error: Steps off a hexagon in a circle with the diameter instead of the radius.

example.question: A regular hexagon is drawn in a circle of radius 30 mm. How long is each side?
example.correct_answer: 30 mm, the same as the radius

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.cause: The diameter is the length the learner measures most often for a circle.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.reveals: Offer "60 mm, the diameter" beside "30 mm, the same as the radius" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.help: Step the compass round the circle at the radius: it fits exactly six times. Join the points.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.feedback: The side of a hexagon in a circle equals the radius.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.error: Sets the compass to less than half the line when bisecting, so the arcs never meet.

example.question: To bisect a line AB with a compass, the radius must be...
example.correct_answer: More than half of AB

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.cause: A small radius feels neater and safer.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.reveals: Offer "Less than half of AB" beside "More than half of AB" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.help: Try both on the board: arcs with a short radius do not cross. Use a radius clearly more than half.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.feedback: Open the compass to more than half the line so the arcs cross.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.error: Uses the full width of a slot as the radius of its semicircular ends.

example.question: A slot is 20 mm wide with semicircular ends. What radius draws each end?
example.correct_answer: 10 mm, half the width

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.cause: The width is the number given, so the learner uses it straight away.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.reveals: Offer "20 mm, the full width" beside "10 mm, half the width" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.help: Draw the centre line, mark the two centres on it, and set the compass to half the width.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.feedback: The radius of a semicircular end is half the width of the slot.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.error: Thinks a 60 degree angle can only be drawn with a protractor.

example.question: How is a 60 degree angle constructed with a compass and a ruler?
example.wrong_answer: It cannot be; a protractor is needed
example.correct_answer: Arc from the end of the line, then the same radius from where it cuts the line; join to the crossing

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.cause: Angles have always been measured with a protractor in the learner's lessons.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.reveals: Offer "It cannot be; a protractor is needed" beside "Arc from the end of the line, then the same radius from where it cuts the line; join to the crossing" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.help: Construct 60 degrees with equal arcs and check it with a protractor; the two agree.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.feedback: Equal arcs make an equilateral triangle, so the angle is 60 degrees.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.GEOM_CONST.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_INSTR.error: Uses the 45 degree set square to draw a 60 degree line.

example.question: Which set square draws a 60 degree line?
example.correct_answer: The 30-60 degree set square

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_INSTR.cause: Both are called set squares and look alike from a distance.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_INSTR.reveals: Offer "The 45 degree set square" beside "The 30-60 degree set square" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_INSTR.help: Hold up both set squares, read the angles at their corners, and draw 30, 45 and 60 degree lines on the T-square.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_INSTR.feedback: The 30-60 degree set square draws 30 and 60 degree lines.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_INSTR.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.error: Slides the T-square stock along any edge of the drawing board, top or bottom.

example.question: Along which edge of the drawing board does the stock of the T-square slide?
example.correct_answer: One straight working edge (the left edge for a right-handed person)

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.cause: All four edges look the same to the learner.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.reveals: Offer "Any edge, top or bottom" beside "One straight working edge (the left edge for a right-handed person)" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.help: Show that only one edge is kept true; using others gives lines that are not parallel.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.feedback: Keep the T-square stock against the one working edge of the board.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLANE_GEOMETRY.DRAW_LAYOU.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.error: Mixes the dimension line with the extension line.

example.question: Which line has arrowheads and shows the size?
example.correct_answer: The dimension line

PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.cause: Both lines are thin and drawn at the same time.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.reveals: Offer "The extension line" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.help: Label a dimensioned drawing: projection (extension) lines come out from the object; the dimension line between them has arrowheads and the number.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.feedback: The dimension line has arrowheads. Extension lines stretch out from the object.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.error: Says drawings are dimensioned in metres.

example.question: In which unit are sizes normally given on a drawing?
example.correct_answer: Millimetres

PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.cause: Building sizes are said in metres, so the learner expects them on drawings.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.reveals: Offer "Metres" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.help: Look at a drawing of a small part: 45 means 45 mm. Most technical drawings use millimetres, stated in a note.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.feedback: Sizes on drawings are normally in millimetres.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.error: Thinks the dimension line is the thick line that shows the shape.

example.question: Which line is thick and shows the shape?
example.correct_answer: The object line

PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.cause: The dimension feels important, so the learner thinks its line must be the thick one.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.reveals: Offer "The dimension line" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.help: Thick lines are only for the object outline; every added line (dimension, projection) is thin.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.feedback: The object line is thick. The dimension line is thin.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.error: Subtracts the sections instead of adding them to find the overall length.

example.question: A part is 30 mm and 45 mm long in two sections. What is the overall length?
example.correct_answer: 75 mm

PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.cause: The learner subtracts the two numbers because "difference" sums are fresh in mind.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.reveals: Offer "15 mm" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.help: Draw the two sections end to end and measure the whole; overall length = sum of the sections.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.feedback: Add the sections: 30 plus 45 is 75 millimetres.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.error: Halves the radius to get the diameter instead of doubling it.

example.question: The radius of a circle is 20 mm. What is the diameter?
example.correct_answer: 40 mm

PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.cause: The learner halves when moving from one circle measure to the other.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.reveals: Offer "10 mm" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.help: Draw a circle with a line through the centre: the diameter is two radii.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.feedback: The diameter is twice the radius: 40 millimetres.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.error: Does not look for the units note, so cannot tell whether 45 means millimetres or centimetres.

example.question: A drawing shows "45" with no unit beside it. How does the reader know the unit?
example.wrong_answer: They guess from the size of the drawing
example.correct_answer: From the note, such as ALL DIMENSIONS IN MILLIMETRES, in the title block

PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.cause: The learner sees bare numbers on a drawing and does not look for the note that gives the unit.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.reveals: Offer "They guess from the size of the drawing" beside "From the note, such as ALL DIMENSIONS IN MILLIMETRES, in the title block" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.help: Find the note "ALL DIMENSIONS IN MILLIMETRES" in the title block; the unit is given once for the whole drawing.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.feedback: A dimension needs a unit, normally millimetres.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.error: Draws projection (extension) lines touching the outline of the object.

example.question: Where does a projection (extension) line start?
example.wrong_answer: Touching the outline of the object
example.correct_answer: A small gap away from the outline

PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.cause: The learner wants the line to look joined to the object.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.reveals: Offer "Touching the outline of the object" beside "A small gap away from the outline" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.help: Show a drawing where touching lines make the outline look bigger; leave a small gap (about 1 to 2 mm).
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.feedback: Leave a small gap between the outline and a projection line.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.error: Mixes up chain and parallel dimensioning.

example.question: Which type of dimensioning measures every size from one datum edge?
example.correct_answer: Parallel (datum) dimensioning

PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.cause: Both types have rows of dimensions, and the names do not say how they are measured.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.reveals: Offer "Chain dimensioning" beside "Parallel (datum) dimensioning" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.help: Draw both on the board: chain links one size to the next; parallel starts every size from the same edge.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.feedback: Parallel dimensioning measures every size from one datum edge.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_TYPES.M_.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.error: Measures a scaled drawing with a ruler instead of reading the dimension written on it.

example.question: A drawing at 1:2 shows a line 25 mm long on the paper, dimensioned 50. What is the real length?
example.wrong_answer: 25 mm, as measured on the paper
example.correct_answer: 50 mm, the dimension written

PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.cause: Measuring with a ruler feels more exact than trusting a number.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.reveals: Offer "25 mm, as measured on the paper" beside "50 mm, the dimension written" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.help: Explain that dimensions always give the real size, whatever the scale; measure, then read the number, and compare.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.feedback: A dimension gives the real size. Read it; do not measure the paper.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.DIMENSIONING.DIM_READ.M_P.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.PLAIN.error: Says 1:50 means the drawing is bigger than the object.

example.question: What does a scale of 1:50 mean?
example.correct_answer: One unit on the drawing stands for 50 on the object

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.PLAIN.cause: The bigger number in 1:50 seems to belong to the drawing.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.PLAIN.reveals: Offer "The drawing is 50 times bigger" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.PLAIN.help: Read 1:50 as "1 on the drawing stands for 50 on the object"; the drawing is smaller.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.PLAIN.feedback: A scale of 1:50 is a reduction: the object is 50 times bigger than the drawing.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.PLAIN.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

example.question: A line is 4 cm on a 1:50 drawing. What is the real length?
example.correct_answer: 4 times 50, which is 200 cm

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.PLAIN.cause: Dividing feels right whenever a scale is used.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.PLAIN.reveals: Offer "0.08 cm (4 divided by 50)" beside "4 times 50, which is 200 cm" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.PLAIN.help: Ask: the drawing is small, the real wall is big; to go from drawing to real, multiply.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.PLAIN.feedback: Multiply the drawing length by 50: 4 times 50 is 200 centimetres.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.PLAIN.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

example.question: What does a scale of 2:1 mean?
example.correct_answer: An enlargement

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.PLAIN.cause: The learner has only met reducing scales.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.PLAIN.reveals: Offer "A reduction" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.PLAIN.help: Draw a small screw at 2:1; it comes out twice as big. The first number is the drawing.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.PLAIN.feedback: A scale of 2:1 makes the drawing twice as big as the object.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.PLAIN.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.error: Divides metres by the scale without converting to millimetres first.

example.question: A wall 6 m long is drawn at 1:50. How long is it on the drawing?
example.correct_answer: 120 mm

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.cause: The learner divides the number given and forgets the unit.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.reveals: Offer "0.12 mm" beside "120 mm" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.help: Write 6 m = 6,000 mm first, then divide by 50. Check: 120 mm fits on a page; 0.12 mm cannot be drawn.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.feedback: Change to millimetres first, then divide by the scale.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.error: Multiplies by the scale for a reduction.

example.question: A bench 2,000 mm long is drawn at 1:20. How long is it on the drawing?
example.correct_answer: 100 mm

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.cause: In other sums the bigger number is multiplied, and the learner does not check the size makes sense.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.reveals: Offer "40,000 mm" beside "100 mm" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.help: Ask: is the drawing smaller or bigger than the bench? Smaller, so divide.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.feedback: For 1:20 the drawing is 20 times smaller: divide by 20.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.error: Divides for an enlargement scale such as 2:1.

example.question: A screw 15 mm long is drawn at 2:1. How long is it on the drawing?
example.correct_answer: 30 mm

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.cause: The learner has only met reducing scales and divides every time.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.reveals: Offer "7.5 mm" beside "30 mm" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.help: Read 2:1 as "2 on the drawing for 1 on the object": twice as big, so multiply by 2.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.feedback: At 2:1 the drawing is twice the real size.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.error: Chooses a scale that makes the drawing bigger than the sheet.

example.question: A room 8 m long is drawn on A4 paper (297 mm long). Which scale fits?
example.correct_answer: 1:50, which makes it 160 mm

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.cause: A larger drawing seems clearer, and the learner does not check the sheet size.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.reveals: Offer "1:10, which makes it 800 mm" beside "1:50, which makes it 160 mm" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.help: Work out the drawing length for 1:10, 1:20 and 1:50 and compare each with 297 mm.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.feedback: Choose a scale that makes the drawing fit inside the border.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.SCALE.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.PLAIN.error: Thinks the small (secondary) divisions of a plain scale are at the right-hand end.

example.question: On a plain scale, where are the small (secondary) divisions?
example.wrong_answer: At the right-hand end, after the last main division
example.correct_answer: To the left of zero, in the first main division

PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.PLAIN.cause: On a ruler the numbers run left to right, so the learner expects the fine part at the end.
PRET.G8.COMMUN.PLAIN_SCALE_DRAWING.PLAIN.reveals: Offer "At the right-hand end, after the last main division" beside "To the left of zero, in the first main division" and ask the child to choose.

PRET.G8.TOOLS_.COMPUTER_SOFTWARE.SOFTWAR.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.TOOLS_.COMPUTER_SOFTWARE.SOFTWAR.error: Calls an application the operating system.

example.question: Which is an operating system?
example.correct_answer: Windows

PRET.G8.TOOLS_.COMPUTER_SOFTWARE.SOFTWAR.cause: The word processor is the program the learner uses most.
PRET.G8.TOOLS_.COMPUTER_SOFTWARE.SOFTWAR.reveals: Offer "A word processor" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
PRET.G8.TOOLS_.COMPUTER_SOFTWARE.SOFTWAR.help: List programs: Windows, Android (run the computer); Word, Excel (do jobs for the user).
PRET.G8.TOOLS_.COMPUTER_SOFTWARE.SOFTWAR.feedback: Windows, Android and Linux are operating systems. A word processor is an application.
PRET.G8.TOOLS_.COMPUTER_SOFTWARE.SOFTWAR.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.TOOLS_.COMPUTER_SOFTWARE.SOFTWAR.error: Picks the wrong application for the task.

example.question: Which application is used for calculations in a table?
example.correct_answer: A spreadsheet

PRET.G8.TOOLS_.COMPUTER_SOFTWARE.SOFTWAR.cause: The learner uses a word processor for everything, including tables.
PRET.G8.TOOLS_.COMPUTER_SOFTWARE.SOFTWAR.reveals: Offer "A word processor" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
PRET.G8.TOOLS_.COMPUTER_SOFTWARE.SOFTWAR.help: Try 12 + 8 in a spreadsheet cell with a formula; a word processor does not calculate.
PRET.G8.TOOLS_.COMPUTER_SOFTWARE.SOFTWAR.feedback: A spreadsheet is used for tables and calculations.
PRET.G8.TOOLS_.COMPUTER_SOFTWARE.SOFTWAR.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.TOOLS_.COMPUTER_SOFTWARE.SOFTWAR.error: Thinks an antivirus is application software like a game.

example.question: An antivirus program belongs to which category of software?
example.correct_answer: Utility (system) software that protects and maintains the computer

PRET.G8.TOOLS_.COMPUTER_SOFTWARE.SOFTWAR.cause: It is installed and opened like any app.
PRET.G8.TOOLS_.COMPUTER_SOFTWARE.SOFTWAR.reveals: Offer "Application software, like a game" beside "Utility (system) software that protects and maintains the computer" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.TOOLS_.COMPUTER_SOFTWARE.SOFTWAR.help: Sort programs by who they serve: the user's jobs (applications) or the computer's care (utilities, operating system).
PRET.G8.TOOLS_.COMPUTER_SOFTWARE.SOFTWAR.feedback: An antivirus is a utility: it looks after the computer.
PRET.G8.TOOLS_.COMPUTER_SOFTWARE.SOFTWAR.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.error: Says only big businesses keep records.

example.question: Which businesses should keep records?
example.correct_answer: Every business, big or small

PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.cause: Small traders around the learner keep money in their heads, so records seem to be for big firms.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.reveals: Offer "Only big businesses" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.help: Ask a small trader how she knows her profit; show a simple daily sales book.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.feedback: Every business keeps records to know its income, spending and profit.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.error: Mixes an asset with a liability.

example.question: A loan owed to a supplier is...
example.correct_answer: A liability

PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.cause: Both words are new and the learner sorts by guess.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.reveals: Offer "An asset" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.help: Two columns: owned by the business (assets: stock, cash, equipment) and owed by the business (liabilities: loans, suppliers).
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.feedback: What a business owes is a liability. What it owns is an asset.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.error: Calls a credit sale a cash sale.

example.question: A customer takes goods and will pay next week. What is this?
example.correct_answer: A credit sale

PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.cause: The goods left the shop, so the sale feels finished as cash.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.reveals: Offer "A cash sale" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.help: Ask "was the money paid now?" Yes: cash sale. Later: credit sale, and the customer is a debtor.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.feedback: A credit sale is paid later. A cash sale is paid now.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.error: Takes total sales as the profit.

example.question: Sales 20,000 shillings, cost of goods sold 12,000, expenses 3,000. What is the net profit?
example.correct_answer: 5,000 shillings

PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.cause: All the money coming in feels like what the business earned.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.reveals: Offer "20,000 shillings" beside "5,000 shillings" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.help: Lay it out: sales - cost of goods = gross profit (8,000); gross profit - expenses = net profit (5,000).
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.feedback: Profit is what is left after costs and expenses, not the sales.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.error: Gives the gross profit as the net profit, forgetting the expenses.

example.question: Gross profit 8,000 shillings, expenses (rent, transport) 3,000. What is the net profit?
example.correct_answer: 5,000 shillings

PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.cause: The learner stops at the first profit line.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.reveals: Offer "8,000 shillings" beside "5,000 shillings" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.help: List the expenses of a kiosk (rent, transport, power); take them away from gross profit.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.error: Adds liabilities to assets to find capital.

example.question: A business has assets of 50,000 shillings and liabilities of 10,000. What is the capital?
example.correct_answer: 40,000 shillings

PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.cause: Adding is the first operation the learner tries with two amounts.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.reveals: Offer "60,000 shillings" beside "40,000 shillings" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.help: Write assets = capital + liabilities; what the business owns, less what it owes, belongs to the owner.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.error: Adds money paid out to the cash balance.

example.question: Cash at the start 2,000, received 5,000, paid out 3,500. What is the cash at the end?
example.correct_answer: 3,500 shillings

PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.cause: The learner adds every amount listed.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.reveals: Offer "10,500 shillings" beside "3,500 shillings" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.help: Use a cash book with two sides: money in, money out. Closing cash = opening + in - out.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.feedback: Money paid out is taken away from the cash.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.FIN_STATEMENT.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.error: Records money the owner takes for the family as a business expense.

example.question: The owner takes 500 shillings from the till to buy food for her family. How is it recorded?
example.correct_answer: As drawings (money taken out by the owner)

PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.cause: The money left the business, and every payment out seems to be an expense.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.reveals: Offer "As a business expense" beside "As drawings (money taken out by the owner)" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.help: Separate business costs (rent, stock, transport) from the owner's own use (drawings); drawings reduce capital, not profit.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.feedback: Money the owner takes for personal use is drawings, not a business expense.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.BOOKKEEPING.BOOKKEEPING.M.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.error: Lists a bill, which is money going out, as a source of income.

example.question: Which is a source of income?
example.correct_answer: A salary

PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.cause: Bills and income both involve money changing hands, and the learner does not ask which way it flows.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.reveals: Offer "A bill" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.help: Draw two arrows: money in (salary, sales, rent received, pocket money) and money out (bills, rent paid, food).
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.feedback: A salary, business profit and sales are income. A bill is spending.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher (MONEY: figures, rates and institution names change; check against current Kenyan practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.error: Thinks a budget is not needed when there is only a little money.

example.question: Why make a budget if you have only a little money?
example.wrong_answer: Budgets are only for people with a lot of money
example.correct_answer: To plan the little money so needs are met and some is saved

PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.cause: Budgets sound like something for people with a lot of money.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.reveals: Offer "Budgets are only for people with a lot of money" beside "To plan the little money so needs are met and some is saved" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.help: Show a learner with 300 shillings for a term planning fare, pens and saving; without a plan it runs out in week 2.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.feedback: A budget plans spending so that needs come first and some is saved.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.error: Thinks moving budget money to personal use is fine if the total stays the same.

example.question: A club treasurer writes "snacks 500" in the budget but spends it on airtime for herself. What is this?
example.wrong_answer: Fine, as long as the total stays the same
example.correct_answer: Unethical: misusing the money and hiding it

PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.cause: The learner thinks honesty is kept if the totals still add up.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.reveals: Offer "Fine, as long as the total stays the same" beside "Unethical: misusing the money and hiding it" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.help: Discuss trust in a club or family: money must be used as the budget says, and changes are agreed openly.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.feedback: Hiding spending or using money meant for something else is unethical.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.error: Calls a budget that spends more than its income balanced.

example.question: Income 3,000 shillings, planned spending 3,400. What is this budget?
example.correct_answer: In deficit by 400 shillings

PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.cause: The learner checks only that every item has a number.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.reveals: Offer "Balanced" beside "In deficit by 400 shillings" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.help: Always subtract: income - spending. A negative answer is a deficit; cut wants until it is zero or more.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.feedback: Spending more than income is a deficit.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.error: Puts wants into a budget before needs.

example.question: Which item goes into a learner's budget first?
example.correct_answer: Bus fare to school

PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.cause: Wants are more exciting to plan for.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.reveals: Offer "A new phone cover" beside "Bus fare to school" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.help: Sort budget cards into needs and wants; fill the budget with needs first, then wants if money is left.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.error: Saves only whatever is left at the end of the month.

example.question: When should saving be put into a budget?
example.wrong_answer: Only if money is left at the end
example.correct_answer: At the start, as a planned item

PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.cause: Saving feels like leftovers, not a need.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.reveals: Offer "Only if money is left at the end" beside "At the start, as a planned item" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.help: Compare two months: saving last (nothing left) and saving first (100 put away); "pay yourself first".
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.feedback: Put saving in the budget at the start, as an item.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.error: Calls money left over in a budget a loss.

example.question: Income 5,000 shillings, spending 4,200. What is the 800 shillings?
example.correct_answer: A surplus, which can be saved

PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.cause: Money "left over" sounds like money not used, so it feels wasted.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.reveals: Offer "A loss" beside "A surplus, which can be saved" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.help: Draw income and spending bars; the part of income not spent is a surplus, ready to save.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.feedback: Money left after planned spending is a surplus.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.error: Treats a loan as income that can be spent freely.

example.question: Wanjiru borrows 1,000 shillings. Should she plan it as free income in her budget?
example.wrong_answer: Yes, it is extra money to spend
example.correct_answer: No, it must be paid back; plan the repayment

PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.cause: Borrowed money is in the hand, so it feels like the learner's own.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.reveals: Offer "Yes, it is extra money to spend" beside "No, it must be paid back; plan the repayment" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.help: Show a budget with the loan as money in and the repayment (with any interest) as money out later.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.feedback: A loan must be paid back. Plan the repayment in the budget.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.INCOME_AND_BUDGETING.BUDG.source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher (MONEY: figures, rates and institution names change; check against current Kenyan practice): a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.error: Says marketing is only selling at the till.

example.question: What does marketing do?
example.wrong_answer: Only takes the money at the till
example.correct_answer: Finds customers and tells them about goods

PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.cause: Selling at the till is the part of marketing the learner sees.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.reveals: Offer "Only takes the money at the till" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.help: Trace how a customer hears of a new shop (poster, friend, radio) before buying: that is marketing.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.feedback: Marketing helps a business find customers and sell.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.error: Relies on the owner's own taste instead of asking customers.

example.question: What is the most reliable way for a new bakery to find out what customers want?
example.wrong_answer: Make what the owner likes best
example.correct_answer: Ask customers through a short survey or interviews

PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.cause: The owner's own taste feels like a good guide to what others want.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.reveals: Offer "Make what the owner likes best" beside "Ask customers through a short survey or interviews" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.help: Run a short class survey on snacks; compare the result with one person's guess.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.feedback: A survey, asking customers and watching competitors give market information.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.error: Ignores how many customers want the goods and can pay when choosing a market.

example.question: Which factor matters most when choosing where to sell school uniforms?
example.correct_answer: Many schools nearby, with customers who can pay

PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.cause: The learner thinks of the seller's wishes, not the buyers.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.reveals: Offer "The seller's favourite town" beside "Many schools nearby, with customers who can pay" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.help: List what a market needs: customers who want the goods and can pay, access, competition, cost of reaching it.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.feedback: Demand, price, location, competition and transport matter in choosing a market.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.error: Thinks the till or other shop equipment is a marketing tool.

example.question: Which is a marketing tool a small shop can use?
example.correct_answer: A poster, a social media page or a radio advert

PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.cause: Anything in a shop seems to help it sell.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.reveals: Offer "A cash register" beside "A poster, a social media page or a radio advert" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.help: Sort shop items into equipment (till, shelves) and marketing tools (posters, signboards, social media pages, radio adverts, samples).
PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.feedback: Posters, radio, social media, samples and offers are marketing tools.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.OF_GOODS_AND_SERVICES.MAR.source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..error: Says intermediaries only raise the price and have no use.

example.question: What does a wholesaler do?
example.correct_answer: Buys in bulk and sells to retailers

PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..cause: The learner hears that middlemen raise prices and does not see the work they do.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..reveals: Offer "Nothing useful" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..help: Follow a bag of maize from a farm to a shop: who stores, transports, breaks bulk and sells it near you?
PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..feedback: Intermediaries bring goods from producers to buyers.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..error: Thinks the direct channel, producer to consumer, is the longest.

example.question: Which is the longest channel?
example.correct_answer: Producer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer

PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..cause: The direct channel has the fewest steps but the learner reads "producer to consumer" as covering the most ground.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..reveals: Offer "Producer to consumer" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..help: Draw each channel with arrows and count the steps; the most intermediaries make the longest channel.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..feedback: The longest channel has a wholesaler and a retailer between producer and consumer.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..source: To confirm by a teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..error: Thinks hoarding goods to raise prices is clever business.

example.question: Which is ethical in distribution?
example.wrong_answer: Hiding goods to raise the price
example.correct_answer: Giving honest weights and fair prices

PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..cause: Higher prices feel like smart business, whatever the method.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..reveals: Offer "Hiding goods to raise the price" next to the right answer and ask the question again in a new context.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..help: Discuss the customer's side of hoarding and false weights; customers leave and the law punishes it.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..feedback: Honest weights, fair prices and safe delivery are ethical. Hoarding and cheating are not.

PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..error: Thinks services cannot have intermediaries, only goods can.

example.question: Which is an intermediary for a service?
example.wrong_answer: None; services always go straight to the customer
example.correct_answer: An M-Pesa agent or an insurance agent

PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..cause: Intermediaries are pictured as people moving goods in lorries.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..reveals: Offer "None; services always go straight to the customer" beside "An M-Pesa agent or an insurance agent" and ask the child to choose.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..help: List services the learner's family uses and who delivers them: agents, booking offices, travel agents.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..feedback: Services also reach customers through agents.
PRET.G8.ENTREP.DISTRIBUTION_OF_GOODS_AN..source: To confirm by a Pre-Technical Studies teacher: a common classroom error, not traced to a study by the author.
